Guardrail: incumbency's automatic Phase-1 bonuses (purse, slots, missio) must never feed back into the score resolveElection uses to defend the SAME seat — only PLATFORMS.likes and fresh backCandidate spend should move that number — so the office pays out in gladiator-facing currency but never discounts the cost of keeping itself.

**Verify first.** Before building: measure how many simulated houses ever clear riseOf(d)>=3 (censusWorth >= 3000 plus fame>=250/favor>=55 plus a full d.rise.standing bar) by, say, week 150-200 across a batch of seeded runs — if eligibility is rare, this is dead weight for most playthroughs and belongs later in the rung ladder or gated lower. Separately, before pricing any term-effect, compute today's resolveElection score spread (base 28-52, +backing up to 44, +9 platform-likes, +ri(0,22) roll — roughly a 75-point swing) against a fame/favor-seeded player base, to confirm a player standing themselves at eligibility isn't already near-guaranteed to win off seeding alone, before a single denarius of Phase-1 campaign spend is added on top.

**#234 — Standing for Office** *(new system)* — **SHIPPED v3.186.0, phases 1-2 plus the cost its risk section demanded.** Both of the item's verify-first questions were answered before a constant was written and the second one changed the design: 71.4% of houses reach rung 3 (median week 80), but the vote as specified was not a contest — the top backing tier won 100.0% at every rung, exactly the dominance the risk section names. The field-growth fix was measured and rejected for punishing the climb; what shipped is an aimed rival answer and `SELF_BACK`, plus `AEDILE_GAMES` on the city's call so a term costs about what buying the seat once costs. Phases 3-5 unbuilt; see the release note.

**#235 — The Fuse, or the Tool: Rework What Debt Actually Survives** *(overhaul)*
ROADMAP.md tells the player, in "The moneylenders," that debt is "entirely survivable if you pay it down — a few hundred a week clears it inside a month." Four hundred lines later, its own v3.50.0 changelog entry — sourced from `test/probes/fuse.mjs`, which still exists and which a fresh rerun still confirms — says a policy that borrows only when short and repays from surplus lives roughly 2.5x shorter under the cheapest lender than a house that never borrows at all, and gets there mostly by hitting the hard lender's clock, not the balance. The two passages describe the same mechanism and can't both be true; the fix already shipped closed one literal bug in the clock's gate and didn't move that ratio.

`src/ludus.jsx`'s `LENDERS` table (line 8466) is exactly as documented: Gratus 3.5%/wk, cap 1400, patience 12, hard; Murena 5.8%/wk, cap 2400, patience 20, soft; Scaeva 8.2%/wk, cap 900, patience 8, hard. `loanWeek` (8504-8556) compounds `owed` every week, and forecloses on `owes(d) > d.loan.principal*4.0 || (L.hard && w >= L.patience+30 && owes(d) > d.loan.principal)` — confirmed at 8552-8553, current source, not the brief's paraphrase. `loanFuse`/`loanClock` (8573-8574) are exactly that gate solved for weeks, and both are printed on the borrow panel at 27871-27872.

ROADMAP.md contradicts itself on what this produces. Line 855 ("The moneylenders," under `## Systems`): "It is entirely survivable if you pay it down — a few hundred a week clears it inside a month." Line 2170-2179, the v3.50.0 changelog entry for issue #163: a rope that "borrows when short and repays everything above its reserve" — never borrowing lives median 156w (16 of 72 alive at 420); servicing Gratus, the cheapest lender, lives median 62w (3 of 72 alive, 30 foreclosed); Scaeva and Murena both read 42w. 156/62 ≈ 2.52x, which is the brief's "roughly 2.5x" and is accurate for Gratus specifically — Murena (soft, 5.8%) is not the cheapest lender by rate, but its bigger cap and no-clock design make it worse in practice, foreclosing via the balance test alone.

I rebuilt `dist/test.html` from current source and reran `test/probes/fuse.mjs 12 300 VERIFY` directly (not from memory of the brief). Directionally it holds: control median life 295w vs. Gratus-serviced 115w (2.57x), 5 of 12 Gratus houses foreclosed, and — the important nuance — all five foreclosed at loan age exactly 43 weeks (`L.patience+30`, +1 tick), meaning `owes(d) > d.loan.principal` was still true for every one of them despite ongoing repayment. Murena (soft) foreclosed 11 of 12 in the same run, via the balance fuse, not a clock. So the fuse is real and current, on both hard lenders and the one soft one, at current numbers.

One correction to the brief: its "already noted" framing — that the earlier release "added an honest in-game warning... but explicitly did not touch the underlying mechanism" — is imprecise. `git log` shows exactly one commit against #163 (567dd73, v3.50.0). It did two things, not one: it added the panel copy (`loanFuse`/`loanClock`, 27871-27872), AND it changed `loanWeek`'s actual foreclosure predicate — the hard clock's `w >= L.patience+30` clause gained `&& owes(d) > d.loan.principal`, closing a real bug where a lender foreclosed a house that had already paid its debt below principal on the same week he foreclosed one that had paid nothing. The commit's own pooled measurement: Gratus foreclosures 42→30 of 72, median life 52→62w. That is a mechanism change, just a narrow one — and my rerun shows why it doesn't rescue the case the brief is about: a house actively using the loan under sustained pressure essentially never gets its balance below principal while still borrowing against it, so the rescue clause almost never fires for exactly the "disciplined but still leaning on debt" player this item is for.

Rework the escalation so debt that is genuinely being serviced earns a real, bounded improvement in survival odds, paid for in capacity rather than given for free — while leaving the balance-based fuse (`owes(d) > principal*4.0`) and the 70%-value man-seizure at `patience+16` (8521-8535) fully intact for a loan that is never serviced. Two levers, both keyed off state the game already half-built: `d.flags.everBorrowed`, set at 8499 the moment a loan clears to zero and read nowhere else in the file (confirmed by grep) — currently a write-only flag. Split it per lender (`d.flags.clearedWith[lender]`) and use it two ways: (1) a lender you have already paid off in full grants a longer hard-clock on your NEXT loan from him, in exchange for a lower cap on that loan — survival, not more capital; (2) a loan that is visibly being paid down (not just idling under interest) can trigger a one-time renegotiation beat at the patience mark, the exact tick `loanWeek` already flags with `d.loan.warned` (8510-8513), offering to buy the same clock extension early at a cost, rather than waiting for a full payoff that a cash-constrained house may never reach. Both levers only ever move the clock and the cap; the rate, the interest owed, and the 4x/70% penalties for a bad-standing loan never change.

*Phases:* 1) **Per-lender good standing (state)** (engine) — Replace the single write-only d.flags.everBorrowed (set at src/ludus.jsx:8499 on every full clearance, read nowhere) with d.flags.clearedWith[lenderKey], set at the same site. Default it inline the way rivalWeekly already defaults d.flags.bayPeak at line 6648 ("d.flags.x = d.flags.x || {}" at point of use), so old saves need no migrate() rewrite. No behavior change yet — this phase only makes the history the rest of the rework reads. 2) **Rework the hard clock and the cap together** (engine) — Introduce loanClockFor(d,L) replacing the bare loanClock(M) call inside loanWeek's foreclosure test (8552-8553) and the panel (27871-27872): returns L.patience+30 normally, L.patience+30+GOOD_STANDING_EXTRA (a tuned constant, sized in phase 5, not guessed) when d.flags.clearedWith[d.loan.who] is set for the loan's own lender. In the same pass, cap the amount borrow() (8481-8489) will accept from an already-cleared lender to a fraction of L.cap (e.g. 0.7x) — the trade the brief names: a longer fuse bought with a smaller loan, not a cheaper or bigger one. The owes(d)>principal*4.0 balance fuse and the patience+16 man-seizure are untouched by this phase, on purpose. 3) **A renegotiation beat, earned not given** (both) — One new EVENTS entry (banner ~17969, same {make(d),run(d,ev,i)} shape as EVENTS.fever at 17986) firing once per loan at loanWeeks(d)===L.patience — the tick loanWeek already marks d.loan.warned at — gated on owes(d) <= d.loan.principal*0.6 (deliberately stricter than the existing missed=1 gate's owes>principal test at 8514, so merely not-yet-in-default doesn't qualify). Two choices: accept the lender's terms (apply phase 2's clock extension to THIS loan early, at a fixed fee or small permanent rate bump) or decline (nothing changes). Touches loanWeek to host the trigger (engine), adds one EVENTS table entry (content) — hence both. 4) **Say the new terms where the money is taken** (content) — Extend the panel block at 27871-27872 (already printing loanFuse(M)/loanClock(M) since #163) with a line that appears once d.flags.clearedWith[k] is true for a lender: the discounted cap and the extended clock for a return loan, in the same voice as the existing #163 copy, so a player who cleared a debt once can read the payoff before borrowing again rather than discovering it in the chronicle log. 5) **Measure it against the same instrument that found the problem** (engine) — Extend test/probes/fuse.mjs (or a sibling probe) with a fourth arm built on the existing loan rope lever in test/harness.mjs (~730-738): once owes(d) is within one week's surplus of zero, pay it off outright instead of only skimming above LAN.reserve(d), so the arm actually reaches clearedWith and takes a second loan. Run at the project's own convention for this system (72 houses x 3+ seeds, per the #163 commit) rather than a single-seed spot check, and pair first-loan vs. good-standing-second-loan median life under the same lender, same seeds. Falsifier: if the gap isn't seed-stable and clearly larger than the 95-248-209w spread the control itself showed across three seeds in the #163 commit, GOOD_STANDING_EXTRA is too small to be a real mechanic.

*Reuses:* LENDERS (8466), loanWeek's full escalation ladder — warned at patience (8510-8513), the missed=1 reputation hit gated on owes(d)>principal (8514-8520), the missed=2 man-seizure at patience+16 taking 70% of gladValue (8521-8535), and the foreclosure predicate (8552-8555) — canBorrow (8560), borrow/repay (8481-8503) including the already-live-but-unread d.flags.everBorrowed set at 8499, loanFuse/loanClock (8573-8574) and their one call site on the borrow panel (27871-27872), the EVENTS {make,run} shape (17971 on; EVENTS.fever at 17986 as the closest two-choice, cost-gated template), chron() (5636), and the project's own inline flags-default-guard idiom (rivalWeekly's d.flags.bayPeak at 6648) for adding save-compatible state without a migrate() rewrite. Test side: test/probes/fuse.mjs's control-vs-arm harness and test/harness.mjs's loan rope (LAN.reserve-gated borrow/repay, ~715-738).

**Risk.** The failure this item can cause is the one its own design-fit note names: a good-standing tier that pays for itself economically — more effective capital, cheaper money, forgiven interest — makes disciplined borrowing the correct way to fund a purchase instead of a real trade-off, turning the loan from a fuse into a bank. That is the same reversal "cruelty is permitted, never optimal" forbids for brutality, applied to credit. Guardrail: every benefit in phases 2-3 is stated in survival terms only — a longer clock, bought with either a smaller next loan or a fee/rate bump on the current one — never a lower rate, forgiven interest, or a bigger cap. The balance fuse and the man-seizure step stay live at their current constants for any loan not in good standing, so a house that never pays down debt is exactly as exposed as it is today. Phase 5's paired measurement is the check on this specifically: if the good-standing arm comes out ahead of a save-only rope on fame, rung, or gold — not just surviving as long as one — the constants have crossed from fuse to bank and need to shrink before shipping, not after.

**Verify first.** Before phases 2-4 ship: (1) rerun test/probes/fuse.mjs fresh at the project's own scale for this system — 72 houses x 3+ seeds, matching the #163 commit's own convention — rather than trusting either the #163 numbers (130+ commits old) or my 12x300x1-seed spot check; (2) confirm the fresh baseline still shows Gratus foreclosures clustering at loan age patience+30(+1) rather than the 4x-balance fuse, the way my rerun did (5 of 5 at loan age 43) — that gap is what GOOD_STANDING_EXTRA has to close, and its size should come off that measurement, not be picked in advance; (3) after implementing, the phase-5 falsifier: paired seeds, same lender, first loan vs. good-standing second loan, median life — not worth keeping unless the improvement is clearly larger than the 95w/248w/209w spread the control itself showed across three seeds in the #163 commit, which is the noise floor this exact instrument already has on record.

**#235 — The Fuse, or the Tool** *(overhaul)* — **ANSWERED v3.187.0, and the answer is not the one it asked for.** Both proposed mechanics were built, measured and reverted against the item's own falsifier: extending the hard clock rescues a fifth of the loans it kills even at +44 weeks (at the clock the median loan owes 1.87x what it took and is climbing), and loosening its escape line to 2x moved 7 houses in 216 against a ~70w control spread. What the item never tested is that every number in #163 came from a rope that always borrowed the lender's whole cap: given a size lever, the cap foreclosed 102 of 216 houses, 700d foreclosed 73, 300d foreclosed 57, monotone in every seed. The loan is not a fuse; taking the maximum is. The panel now prices each amount, and three stale passages are corrected. The good-standing tier is not built and the release note says why.

**#236 — Rivals Roll Dice; They Don't Read Your Roster** *(overhaul)* — **SHIPPED v3.190.0.** Three of its four verify-first checks passed and the fourth failed for a reason outside the item: `RIVAL_SEED` names three fixed houses, only one of which (Tullius) has train or bid above baseline, so an aimed move reaches the log once every 92 weeks against the item's 40-week target. Recorded rather than tuned around. The read itself is calibrated — four houses past the 40% landing target, the rest at the uniform floor — and the win-rate delta is +0.17 points. See the release note.
RIVAL_MOVES.retrain (src/ludus.jsx:6511-6517) sends a man to one of the five classes he isn't already with a bare pick() — a 20% floor on landing anywhere in particular. RIVAL_MOVES.buy (6478-6493) always lifts whoever tops gladValue() off the block, full stop. Both run inside an engine whose whole identity is a six-class cycle (COUNTERS, line 384) worth a real 1.15/0.91 damage multiplier (CLS_EDGE, line 387, spent at 10067 and 17214) — and across every rival-house system in the file, nothing has ever once looked at what the player is actually fielding to decide which way to lean.

Verified against source: RIVAL_MOVES.retrain.run (6511-6517) does `const to = pick(Object.keys(CLASSES).filter(c=>c!==was))` — uniform over the five other classes, no argument passed in that could see the player's roster. RIVAL_MOVES.buy.run (6478-6493) does `d.market.filter(g=>!isAuctor(g)).sort((a,b)=>gladValue(b)-gladValue(a))[0]` — pure value sort, class untouched. Both fire out of rivalTurn (6571-6590), which only reads d.rivals and d.market. The nearby poaching system was the other candidate for "reads the player's men" and it does read them (poachTarget, 12600-12604) — but only g.defiance and gladValue, never g.cls. No classMix/classCounts-style helper exists anywhere in the file (grepped, zero hits). So the brief's claim holds exactly: the six-class cycle that CLS_EDGE and power()'s smaller 1.045 counter-nudge (9448) make real and mechanical in every player bout is invisible to the two rival moves — and to the house-selection weighting around them — that would need to see it to press on it. A house can grind at you for 300 weeks without ever having built the one class that would hurt you specifically.

Give rivalTurn a cheap read of the player before retrain/buy choose a class, and make how sharp that read is a function of personality data that already exists. Concretely: tally activeG(d) by .cls, weighted toward men with recent g.lastFought (a real per-fighter field, confirmed at 5678 and used for "fought this week" staleness checks throughout week resolution) to name the player's dominant class; reverse-walk COUNTERS with the same idiom the UI already uses at line 26354 (`Object.keys(COUNTERS).find(k=>COUNTERS[k]===dominant)`) to name the class that beats it. Then give retrain.run and buy.run a lanista-scaled chance to take that class instead of the current fully-random or pure-value pick — scaled off lanistaOf(h.name).train and .bid respectively, which are not new numbers: they are the exact fields that already decide how often retrain and buy fire at all (retrain weight is literally `lanistaOf(h.name).train`; buy weight is `1+(bid-1)*2`). Tullius (train 1.55, bid 1.6, "who is simply better at this") and Rufinus (train 1.50, "who says nothing at all") read you sharply; Glaber (train 0.75, "who bought it all at once") and Solonius (train 1.0, bid 1.0, a schemer whose competence stats are baseline) barely read you at all — the personality differentiation the brief asked to confirm is plausible was already sitting in LANISTAE (1912-1943), unused for this. Pair every biased pick with a new flavor-line branch fed through the existing d.rivalLog/chron pipeline (rivalTurn already does `d.rivalLog=[...].slice(0,8); chron(d,line,"info")`) and rendered by the existing "The other houses" Sect (22866-22878) — no new UI surface, just a second string in the pick([...]) arrays retrain.run and buy.run already use.

*Phases:* 1) **Roster-read helper + reverse-counter lookup** (engine) — A new pure function near RIVAL_MOVES (e.g. rivalReadOf(d)) that tallies activeG(d) by .cls, weighted toward fighters with recent g.lastFought, to name the player's dominant class, plus a reverse-COUNTERS lookup (reusing the exact idiom already at line 26354) to name the class that beats it. No behavior change yet — pure plumbing, callable and checkable in isolation before anything consumes it. 2) **Bias retrain, ship its tell in the same diff** (both) — RIVAL_MOVES.retrain.run's uniform pick(Object.keys(CLASSES).filter(c=>c!==was)) gains a lanistaOf(h.name).train-scaled chance to take the countering class from Phase 1 instead; a new branch in its existing pick([...]) flavor lines fires specifically when that happened, landing in d.rivalLog/chron the same week the bias takes effect — no separate follow-up phase for legibility. 3) **Bias buy, ship its tell in the same diff** (both) — RIVAL_MOVES.buy.run's plain gladValue(b)-gladValue(a) sort gains a lanistaOf(h.name).bid-scaled tilt toward a d.market fighter whose class counters the player's dominant class, bounded by a value-tolerance band so it stays a soft preference rather than starving player market choice; matching new flavor-line branch shipped in the same diff. 4) **Calibrate the read-sharpness curve against measured data** (content) — Numeric tuning of the train/bid-to-read-chance mapping and the buy value-tolerance band, driven by a probes/-style measurement script (matching the file's own probes/works.mjs and 900-bout precedents) rather than hand-picked constants — answers verify_first's four checks with real numbers before the feature is called done.

*Reuses:* activeG(d) (3732); g.lastFought (per-fighter, set throughout week resolution e.g. 14160, 16657, 16827); COUNTERS (384) and its reverse-lookup idiom already live at 26354; CLASSES[cls].key (376-383); lanistaOf(h.name).train and .bid (1912-1945, already the retrain/buy firing-frequency weights at 6511 and 6478); RIVAL_MOVES.retrain.run and .buy.run themselves (6511-6517, 6478-6493), including their existing pick([...]) flavor-string idiom; d.market and gladValue (3772) for the buy-side candidate pool; d.rivalLog + chron() (6588-6589) and the "The other houses" Sect (22866-22878) as the tell's delivery channel, all with zero new state or UI.

**Risk.** The brief's own named risk is right: a house that silently out-counters you off-screen is indistinguishable from the engine just getting harder, which is exactly the failure the file's own audit item #230 describes (comment at 9802-9821) — two independently-typed copies of the same missio-odds formula that agreed today but could silently drift, against the engine's own stated commitment that "the box is never a surprise." (Correction to the brief: that precedent is #230/#150, not a "crux/appeal" incident — I could not find a crux/appeal-specific version of this failure in the source, but #230 is the same family of bug and is directly verified.) The guardrail is structural, not a promise to remember later: Phases 2 and 3 below ship the biased pick and its tell line in the same diff, in the same run() function, so there is no commit where the logic exists without the line that names it. Second-order risk: because train/bid already gate move frequency, a high-train house both fires retrain more often AND reads sharper when it does — the two effects compound multiplicatively and could make Tullius-tier houses swing from "aggressive" to "reads you like a book" all at once. Guardrail: cap the read-chance well under 1.0 (clamp, not open-ended) so even a maximally shrewd lanista is a strong bias, never a certainty, and a player who diversifies class mix mid-campaign can still dodge it.

**Verify first.** (1) Baseline collision: uniform retrain already lands on the specific counter-class ~20% of the time (1 of 5 non-current classes) by chance alone. Measure whether the biased version pushes high-train houses meaningfully past that floor (target ballpark ≥40%) while low-train houses (Glaber 0.75, Pollio 0.85) stay close to baseline — if they don't diverge, the "sharper lanista" premise is cosmetic. (2) Tell frequency: rivalTurn only acts on 30% of weeks (`if(R()>0.7) return`) and retrain/buy are two of nine weighted moves in RM_KEYS — run the file's own kind of measured simulation (it already cites "measured across 900 bouts" at 6417 and a probes/works.mjs precedent at 6599) to count how many counter-motivated retrain/buy events actually reach d.rivalLog per campaign; if it's roughly one every 40+ weeks the tell reads as a fluke, not a pattern. (3) Win-rate delta: quantify how much the biased buy/retrain moves the player's bout win% against a house that's had several stable weeks to react, and compare that shift's magnitude against the existing CLS_EDGE (1.15/0.91) and power() (1.045) counter effects already tuned into every bout — the new pressure must stay additive-and-survivable, not stack into something CLS_EDGE alone doesn't already produce. (4) Cheapest signal first: check whether lastFought-recency-weighting the class tally actually changes the dominant-class answer often enough to justify the extra complexity over a plain activeG(d) tally by .cls — only keep the recency weighting if a player benching a class without retraining it away is a common enough case to matter.

**#237 — The Heir You Actually Have** *(overhaul)* — **SHIPPED, v3.180.0 + v3.181.0.** The identity fix (`eligibleSons`, `nameHeir` carrying a real `cid`, the multi-son chooser), the passed-over son's name surviving into the forebear record and a chronicle line, and the toga trigger recognizing an already-named son all landed. Phase 4's low-probability grudge hook was deliberately dropped — nothing reads it, and a write-only flag is exactly the dead-state fault this project's checks hunt down. Phase 5 landed as toga-moment awareness rather than static `HEIRS.son` text variants — the chooser row already prints the boy's age, and the toga is the one place the distinction actually plays out.
heirEligible already checks a real, named boy's age before it lets you pick "A son" — livingKids(d).some(c=&gt;c.sex==="m" &amp;&amp; childAge(d,c)&gt;=9) — but nameHeir("son") never looks him up; it hands you a stranger pulled from PRAENOMINA/NOMINA/COGNOMINA, the identical fabrication branch used for "nephew," an heir kind for which no real candidate has ever existed in game state. Meanwhile the toga-at-16 "scion" path already builds the correct object — {cid, traits, mentorId} — by calling straight into d.domus.children; nameHeir just never learned the trick.

heirEligible (HELPERS, next to the HEIRS table) gates the "son" option correctly: `d.lanista.age>=40 && livingKids(d).some(c=>c.sex==="m" && childAge(d,c)>=SON_AGE)`, SON_AGE=9, against a real child object living in d.domus.children with its own id, born week, and up:{palus,rhetor,box} raising counters accrued by raiseEvent at ages 7 and 12. That boy is real, simulated, and already producing chronicle beats through childYear() at 3/5/9/14. But nameHeir(d,kind) — the only function that ever turns a chosen kind into d.heir — resolves the name for "son" through the exact same line as "nephew": `kind==="doctore" && d.doctore ? d.doctore.name : `${pick(PRAENOMINA)} ${pick(NOMINA)} ${pick(COGNOMINA)}``. It writes no cid, no traits, no mentorId. One correction to the brief: "nephew" fabricating a name is not a bug — grepping the whole file for brother/nephew state turns up no tracked NPC anywhere (ties, kin, rivals, patrons); there is no real nephew to consult, so nameHeir("nephew") is working exactly as intended. "son" is the one kind that promises a real person and delivers a stranger. A second correction, in nameHeir/succeed()'s favor: the brief worried succeed() itself would need surgery, but succeed() already reads d.heir.cid/mentorId/traits/palusRaised generically (mentor morale+regard bump, tookHouse stamp on the matching child) — that block was written for the "scion" kind (set directly by resolveToga, which builds `{kind:"scion", cid:c.id, traits:heirTraitsFromUp(up), mentorId, mentorName}` and never even calls nameHeir — heirEligible(d) never returns "scion", so nameHeir is in practice invoked only for son/nephew/doctore, exclusively from chooseHeir(kind)=>mut(d=>nameHeir(d,kind)) on the House sheet's button row). succeed() needs zero changes: the entire gap is that nameHeir("son") never builds the object shape resolveToga already builds. Downstream, succeed() unconditionally archives d.domus (`fam = {wife, children: domus.children.slice()}` whenever a wife or any children exist, regardless of d.heir.kind) and resets it to {wife:null, children:[], nextKin:1}; the only trace kept in d.forebears is `children: fam.children.length` — a bare integer, not even names. The single per-child fact that survives is c.tookHouse=d.week, set only for the child matching d.heir.cid — and "son" heirs, uniquely among the four kinds, never set a cid, so the real boy who made the option eligible in the first place is stamped exactly like his unnamed siblings and disappears into a headcount. A further concrete case beyond the brief: a 16-year-old who answered togaEvent's "Not yet — let him prove himself first" keeps c.grown=false and c.togaTil set, but he still satisfies heirEligible's blunter age>=9 "son" check the whole time he's on that cooldown — so a fully raised, mentor-bonded boy the game is actively narrating can be discarded for a random stranger with one click on the House sheet, while his own toga event is still pending.

Give nameHeir a cid the same way resolveToga already does, and stop treating "son" as a name-pool draw. Add eligibleSons(d) beside heirEligible — the same age/sex/living filter, but returning the actual candidate child objects (id, name, age, mentorId/mentorName, and heirTraitsFromUp(c.up) computed off whatever up-raising he already has, which is legitimate data as early as age 9 since raiseEvent's stage 1 resolves at 7). heirEligible itself keeps its existing string-array contract (its return value feeds a UI-freshness signature at the "villa" joinSig and a boolean branch check, both of which only care whether "son" is present, not who) but internally calls eligibleSons(d).length>0 instead of duplicating the .some() check. nameHeir(d,"son",cid) then resolves the real child — defaulting to the sole eligible boy when cid is omitted and only one qualifies, for callers that don't yet pass one — and writes d.heir in the same shape resolveToga uses for scion: {kind:"son", name:c.name, cid:c.id, traits:heirTraitsFromUp(c.up), palusRaised, mentorId, mentorName}. Kind stays "son," not "scion" — HEIRS.son keeps its own, weaker numbers (fameKeep 0.72, unrest +6) against HEIRS.scion's (0.86, -4), so an early handover under duress remains mechanically rougher than a clean toga-at-16 succession; only the identity plumbing is unified, not the payout. On the House sheet, when eligibleSons(d) has more than one boy, the single generic "A son" button becomes one row per real boy (reusing the name/age/"at X's shoulder" mentor line already rendered for kids.map in the blood-of-the-house panel), each wired to chooseHeir("son", c.id); with exactly one eligible boy the button collapses to his real name instead of the generic HEIRS.son.name label. Last, a passed-over eligible son stops disappearing into a bare integer: when nameHeir names a different kind while eligibleSons(d) is non-empty, or when succeed() archives a domus containing an unnamed eligible son, keep his name and a defiance/grudge seed in the forebears record instead of just incrementing children.length — a low-probability hook a later week can read (mirroring the grudge field rival houses already carry, and the pattern bayRefill uses to open a new house on the bay) rather than a guaranteed storyline.

*Phases:* 1) **eligibleSons helper** (engine) — New eligibleSons(d) beside heirEligible returning the real candidate child objects (id, name, age, mentorId/mentorName, heirTraitsFromUp(c.up)); heirEligible's own return contract (string array) is unchanged but its son-check is rewritten to call eligibleSons(d).length>0, removing the duplicated .some() logic. 2) **nameHeir carries a cid** (engine) — nameHeir(d, kind, cid) resolves a real child for kind==='son' via domusOf(d).children.find(c=>c.id===cid) (defaulting to the sole eligible boy when cid is omitted and exactly one qualifies) and writes d.heir in the same shape resolveToga already builds for scion — {kind:'son', name:c.name, cid:c.id, traits, palusRaised, mentorId, mentorName} — leaving nephew/doctore and HEIRS.son's numeric fields untouched; succeed() requires no edits. 3) **House sheet chooser** (both) — chooseHeir(kind, cid) and the 'After you' button row on the House sheet render one row per eligibleSons(d) boy (name, age, mentor line, reusing the kids.map pattern already used in the blood-of-the-house panel) when more than one qualifies, and substitute the sole boy's real name for the generic 'A son' label when exactly one does. 4) **passed-over son consequence** (both) — When nameHeir names a non-matching kind, or succeed() archives a domus with an unnamed eligible son still in it, capture his name (not just a headcount) in the forebears record and seed a low-probability grudge/defiance hook a later week can read, on the pattern of the rival-house grudge field and bayRefill's new-house spawn — background texture, not a mandatory storyline. 5) **flavor text pass** (content) — Age-aware variants of HEIRS.son's line/took text for a boy named heir well before 16 (distinct in tone from the clean toga-at-16 scion handover), plus the chron() line(s) for a passed-over son now that his name, not just a count, survives into the record.

*Reuses:* heirEligible, nameHeir, HEIRS (son/nephew/doctore/scion), succeed, resolveToga/togaEvent/heirTraitsFromUp (the pattern being ported), domusOf, livingKids, childAge, SON_AGE, CHILD_YEARS, chooseHeir/mut, d.domus.children's existing fields (id, name, sex, born, up:{palus,rhetor,box}, mentorId, mentorName, grown, togaTil, wed, dead), d.forebears, the rival-house grudge field and bayRefill/NEW_HOUSES spawn pattern for the passed-over-son hook.

**Risk.** If the identity carry-over quietly comes with HEIRS.son's numbers rising to meet scion's, "who do you name heir" stops being a real trade-off — a raised, mentor-bonded, real-named son would strictly dominate nephew (900 gold, +12 unrest, no bond) and doctore (best morale/unrest but weakest fameKeep) in every case, and the game loses a decision it currently protects by making every heir option a different cost. Guardrail: this item touches only nameHeir's identity plumbing and eligibleSons/the chooser UI — HEIRS.son's fameKeep/favorKeep/unrest/morale/gold fields are explicitly out of scope, so scion (wait for the toga) stays strictly better numerically than an early-named son, which keeps patience the stronger play. A second, smaller risk on the "passed-over consequence" phase: turning a quiet simulation detail into a mandatory rival-house storyline the player must chase would work against "the ludus is the game" (family texture, not a new operated system) — guardrail: keep the seed probabilistic and background, on the bayRefill/grudge model, never a required follow-up quest.

**Verify first.** Instrument nameHeir/resolveToga to log d.heir.kind on every call and re-run the existing probes/scion.mjs-style harness (already referenced in the #226 audit comment) across a large sample of simulated houses/weeks to get a real number for how often the currently-broken "son" branch is actually chosen versus players simply waiting for the toga to fire on its own — a low hit-rate doesn't invalidate the coherence argument (the brief's own "men are not units" standard doesn't need volume to be violated), but it sizes this against the other nine survey items. Same harness should confirm, with a number, whether the togaTil-cooldown overlap case (a real 16-year-old eligible via "son" while his own toga event is pending) occurs in practice at nonzero frequency, and what fraction of houses ever have 2+ sons simultaneously eligible — if multi-son households are vanishingly rare, phase 3's per-boy chooser row may be overbuilt against a simpler single-name substitution.

**#238 — Damnatio Ad Ludum Doesn't End In Freedom** *(overhaul, discretionary)* — **SHIPPED v3.191.0.** Its premise held and its diagnosis moved a layer down: the discharge does not merely fail to pay, it barely happens — 1 of 45 under the reference player, 12 of 82 (14.6%) under determined play, and 0 of those 12 ever crossed the rudis bar. Its proposed curve was inverted by the data: surviving and winning are opposed strategies here, so the term carries most of the discount and how well he fought adds to it. Phase 5's retune of CRIMES declined with the reason. See the release note.
The game's own banner comment over the feature states its whole point: a man condemned to the ludus who "survived his term earned the rudis out of it." `damnCheck` fires when that term clears, gives him a regard/morale bump — and leaves `g.status` at `"active"`. Its own chronicle line even says so out loud: he is "a gladiator of this house like any other, which is a sentence of a different kind and he knows it." The discharge the feature is named for is mechanically identical to doing nothing.

`isDamn`/`damnLeft`/`makeDamnatus`/`damnArrive`/`damnCheck` (src/ludus.jsx 1536-1572) run the sentence: `damnLeft(g) = g.damnatus.bouts - (g.wins+g.losses)`, counted in total bouts fought, not wins. The six `CRIMES` (1528-1535) carry terms of 10-18 bouts. When `damnLeft(g)<=0`, `damnCheck` clears `g.damnatus`, adds +26 regard/+24 morale/+6 mercy-rep/-6 unrest, logs a `"servedOut"` memory (flavor-only, weight 18, no further mechanical effect), and returns — `g.status` is never touched. He is still owned, still sellable the instant he's discharged (`sellG`'s only guard is `isDamn(g)`, 25505), still subject to everything a bought man is.
Actual freedom runs through a completely separate function, `grantRudis` (19802-19854), gated on `rudisEligible(g) = !isAuctor(g) && g.wins>=RUDIS_WINS(10) && g.pfame>=RUDIS_FAME(180)` (5597-5598) — and `rudisEligible` excludes only `isAuctor`, not `isDamn`. A discharged damnatus is judged on literally the same predicate as a purchased man, priced at `rudisCost` (max(40, gladValue*0.20 + house-scaled overhead)), and only `grantRudis` sets `g.status="freed"`, pushes the `d.freed`/annals-`"freed"` entry that `houseRecord(d).freed` counts toward the `closed` mercy ending (19559), and triggers the fame/unrest/defiance/doctore payoff a real manumission carries.
The two counters don't even measure the same thing: a sentence is satisfied by 10-18 *bouts fought*, win or lose; the rudis wants 10 *wins* specifically plus 180 renown. A damnatus who loses even one bout in a 10-bout term already falls short of RUDIS_WINS the moment his sentence ends, before renown is even considered — and the code's own measurement (19533-19558) states plainly that a free-able man "is by definition one who has fought a great deal," with `rudisEligible` crossed by only 14.1% of every man who ever draws breath in a house, about four per house over 400 weeks (2912-2917). Nothing in `damnCheck` adds a win or a point of pfame. So "fight out your sentence and earn the rudis for it" is a narrative promise the mechanics never pay.
One correction to the survey brief: taking damnati does not cost the house a fee. The `damnatio` event (18754-18773) pays the house `rnd(60+n*45)` denarii to accept 1-2 condemned men and raises the accepting magistrate patron's favor by +8 (-7 if refused) — there is no gold cost at intake. The real, verified cost is non-monetary: `damnArrive` docks the rest of the active roster -5 morale/-4 regard and +4 unrest per arrival, and accepting nudges the house's "blood" reputation axis +4 (one of four competing house identities in `REP_ORDER`, opposite "mercy") — plus the men arrive with depressed morale (22-40), defiance (8-26), regard (30-46) and potential (-12), and can't be sold until discharged.

Give the discharge check in `damnCheck` a second effect beyond the regard/morale/rep bump it already has, keyed to how he served — computed with no new state, since `genGladiator` seeds `wins:0, losses:0` so his win rate at discharge (`g.wins / Math.max(1, g.wins+g.losses)`) is exactly his win rate over the sentence.
Primary branch (recommended): attach a personal, one-time discount to his own `rudisEligible` bar — `g.rudisDischarge = {wins, fame}`, scaled down from RUDIS_WINS/RUDIS_FAME by his win rate, floored so it never exceeds the standard bar. He remains owned and fightable (still a fully productive, still-dangerous-if-talented gladiator, per the game's own defiance-scales-with-talent value) but the road to his actual freedom via the existing `grantRudis` is now shorter in proportion to how honorably he served, not identical to a bought man's.
Fallback branch: fire a leaner version of `grantRudis`'s freedom effects directly from `damnCheck` when the term clears — `g.status="freed"`, the fame/unrest/defiance payoff, no `rudisCost` charge (the state already took its price in the fixed term). This matches the narrative claim literally but needs the guardrail in design_risk below, because unlike an earned rudis it requires no wins at all, only survival.
Either way this is one new conditional inside the existing discharge/rudis-grant pair — `damnCheck` gains a branch, `rudisEligible`/`rudisStanding`/`rudisWord` gain a per-man override read — not a new subsystem, matching how the brief scoped it.

*Phases:* 1) **Measure the discharge gap** (engine) — A probes-style script (companion to the existing probes/quote.mjs, referenced at line 19807) run over the same houses-x-weeks scale the code's own balance comments use, reporting for every damnatus who reaches damnLeft(g)<=0 alive: win rate over the sentence, wins/pfame at discharge vs RUDIS_WINS/RUDIS_FAME, and bouts/weeks (if any) until he independently clears rudisEligible afterward — the real numbers needed to size the discount curve or choose outright-vs-discount. 2) **Branch the discharge check** (engine) — Extend damnCheck (~1559) to compute rate = g.wins/Math.max(1,g.wins+g.losses) when the term clears and attach a per-man override (e.g. g.rudisDischarge = {wins,fame}) sized from phase 1's numbers; thread that override through rudisEligible, rudisStanding, and rudisWord (5598-5623), floored so it never exceeds the standard bar. 3) **Chronicle the two outcomes** (content) — Replace damnCheck's single fixed chron() line (1570) with rate-banded variants distinguishing a man who served well from one who merely survived, matching the per-crime specificity already used at intake in the CRIMES table. 4) **Guard the freedom accounting** (engine) — Confirm grantRudis's existing payoff (fame, unrest, defiance, mercy rep, offerDoctore, the d.freed/annals fate='freed' entry read by houseRecord and the closed-ending gate at 19559) fires unchanged when a discounted man later clears the bar through it — the discount only moves the gate. If the fallback outright-grant branch is built instead, tag its annals fate distinctly from ordinary 'freed' so houseRecord(d).freed is not inflated by a channel that only requires survival, not wins. 5) **Retune the sentence lengths** (content) — Once phase 1's numbers exist, revisit CRIMES' bouts field (currently 10-18, set with no reference to RUDIS_WINS/RUDIS_FAME) so term length and the discount curve agree on what 'served honourably' actually costs a man in practice.

*Reuses:* isDamn, damnLeft, makeDamnatus, damnArrive, damnCheck, CRIMES (1528-1572); RUDIS_WINS, RUDIS_FAME, RUDIS_AGE, rudisEligible, rudisStanding, rudisWord (5597-5623); grantRudis, rudisCost, canAffordRudis, offerDoctore (19794-19854); annalsClose/annalsSync, houseRecord, the `closed` ending gate at 19559; addRep with the "mercy"/"blood" REP_ORDER axes (2295, 18772); the existing `probes/quote.mjs` pattern referenced at 19807 as the template for a phase-1 measurement script; chron() for new discharge lines.

**Risk.** The fallback (outright-grant) branch is the sharp edge. `damnLeft` only requires surviving 10-18 bouts, not winning them, and intake is a net gold gain to the house, not a cost — so an unconditional outright grant would make damnatio a cheaper, faster, effort-free route to the exact `houseRecord(d).freed>=5` count the `closed` ending's own measurement comment (19533-19558) calibrated as rare on purpose (2 of 20 simulated houses ever clear the ordinary rudis bar; the mercy ending is deliberately hard-won). That directly undercuts "mercy is mechanically the strongest long game" by making it mechanically the *cheapest* game instead, through a channel the design never routes through combat performance at all.
Guardrail: if the outright branch is built, do not record it with `fate:"freed"` in `annalsClose`/`annalsSync` — give it a distinct fate (e.g. `"servedOut"`) so it doesn't feed `houseRecord(d).freed` and the `closed` gate, preserving the calibration the code already measured. The discount branch avoids this risk structurally, since it only narrows the same rudisEligible/grantRudis path everything else uses — a discharged man still has to fight and win to actually walk free — which is the reason to prefer it as the default.

**Verify first.** Before writing either branch: probe, over the same houses-x-weeks scale the code's own comments already use (e.g. 12-20 houses, 400-600 weeks), every damnatus who reaches `damnLeft(g)<=0` alive, and log his win rate at discharge and his wins/pfame gap to RUDIS_WINS/RUDIS_FAME at that moment, plus how many further bouts (if any) it takes him to independently clear `rudisEligible` afterward under the CURRENT code. Two falsifiable outcomes: (a) if discharged damnati already clear `rudisEligible` at a materially higher rate than ordinary bought men over an equivalent stretch — plausible, since `damnCheck`'s existing +26 regard/+24 morale could be indirectly helping him survive to accumulate wins later — the "essentially never happens" premise needs revisiting and a smaller fix (e.g. nothing, or just surfacing his distance to the bar in the UI) may suffice; (b) if, as the code's own 14.1%-of-all-men measurement suggests, discharged damnati essentially never cross the bar either, that confirms the premise and hands phase 1 the exact numbers (average wins/pfame short, by win-rate band) needed to size the discount curve rather than guessing it.

**#239 — A Life Outside the Wall** *(new system, discretionary)*
The `woman` ask in `ASKS` is the only place in a 31,100-line file that admits a gladiator has a life past the gate, and winning it does exactly one thing: it sets `g.flags = 1`, a field the file never reads again except to stop the ask firing twice. A few thousand lines away, `d.domus` runs a wife, a dowry economy, a conception roll, and a four-stage raising arc for the one man in the house guaranteed never to fight — while the men who actually bleed for it get a flag. Give the thread a body: an object on the man, a second person the house can lose, and a name for the chronicle to hang his death on.

Verified directly: `ASKS.woman` (src/ludus.jsx:13657-13664) gates on `g.wins>=6 && regardOf(g)>=55 && !g.flags`, and its `yes` branch runs `g.flags = 1; g.regard += 18; g.morale += 14; g.defiance += 6`. A full-file search for `.flags\b` (285 hits) turns up exactly one non-`d.flags`/`S.flags` occurrence: this pair, one write at 13660 and one read at 13657 — and that read is the ask's own re-fire gate, not a second consumer. Nothing else in the file — no UI card, no chronicle line, no defiance/despair check, no death-time reaction — ever looks at it. Unlike every other entry in `ASKS`, `yes`/`no` here don't even call `remember(d,g,kind)` into the REGARD/`g.memory` system (compare `brother`'s `remember(d,g,"kept")` at 13621) — the stat bump is applied by hand and leaves no trace in the man's own memory log. It is also the lowest-weighted of the five ASKS entries (`w:6`, against `brother:10`, `match:9`, `year:8`, `burial:7`), so it is both the cheapest possible payoff in that table and the one most rarely rolled.

Meanwhile `d.domus` (8002-8252) runs a fully simulated household for the lanista alone: `marryReady` (age<56, rise>=1 or fame>=60) gates a weekly 10% `matchEvent` roll among three dowry-priced candidates; a married house rolls conception at 6%/week once wife<40, fewer than 3 living kids, and 6+ weeks since the last birth (`bearChild`, 8047); `familyWeek` (8200) advances each child through unforced "years between the gates" narration at ages 3/5/9/14 (`childYear`, `CHILD_YEARS=[3,5,9,14]`) and three forced choice-gates — `raiseEvent`/`resolveRaise` at 7 and 12 (palus/rhetor/box, the palus branch pairing the boy with a veteran mentor who gets a `regard`/`morale` bump), `togaEvent`/`resolveToga` naming him `d.heir` at 16, `daughterEvent`/`resolveDaughter` marrying a daughter off at 15 to a patron, a rival (folding a feud — `weddingEndsFeud`), or a merchant house for dowry. The lanista is the one man never at risk on the sand, and he is the only one the file bothers to give a family to.

Replace the flat flag with a persisting object on the man — `g.family = { partner, child, kind, since }` — seeded by winning the `woman` ask (or a widened trigger; the ask's own `need` has no gender gate on `g`, and its text already runs through `her(text,g)` for a gladiatrix, so the new object has to handle a same-sex pairing without a `bearChild`-style conception path, not exclude it). It is not a tie: `d.ties`/`addTie` (4469-4650) links two roster IDs, and there is no "outside the wall" analog anywhere in the file — this is new state shaped like the domus's own `c` child records (`up`, `mentorId`, `born`), not like `tieList`.

Four hooks, each reusing a real, already-verified mechanism:
1. **It can deepen.** A weekly low-roll check in the man's own upkeep pass (parallel to `bearChild`'s 6%/week gate) can produce a child on the thread; age it the same way `childAge`/`CHILD_YEARS` age a domus child, without the four forced life-gates (a gladiator's yard has no `rhetor`/`box`/`toga` — his boy doesn't inherit a ludus).
2. **A grown child can walk in at the gate.** `kinWeek`/`raiseKin` (14402-14432) is the literal precedent the brief points at: a fallen man's kin arrives, inherits his `cls`/`kit`, draws a trait from `KIN_TRAITS`, and joins with `g.sworn = {how:"proper",...}` — vengeful or not, keyed off `d.fallen`. A grown thread-child reaching draft age is the same shape keyed off `g.family` instead of `d.fallen`, whether the father is alive or dead.
3. **A rival can threaten it.** `startPoach`/`defect`/`poachWeek` (12600-12671) already target `g.defiance>=45` men and the live `poached` arc's bait line is literally "freedom in three years... and a bed of his own" (18320-18345). A man with `g.family` set is either a sharper poach target (leverage: the family, not the man, is what's dangled) or the bait text branches on it — no new subsystem, a new read on an existing one.
4. **It can pull on `freedom`.** `AMBITIONS.freedom` (1719-1724) is "To hold the rudis before he is thirty" with its own `ask`/`press`/`despair` text keyed through the player-initiated `WORDS.wants` conversation (13688-13701), entirely separate from `ASKS`. A man with `g.family` gets a second, harder-edged reason to press it — the existing `press`/`despair` copy can vary on `g.family` being set without a new ambition kind.
5. **His death names them.** `boutAftermath`'s death branch (17431-17457) already runs `mournKin`/`kinReact`/`dropTies` and chronicles who was watching. One more `chron()` line reading `g.family` — "He leaves a woman in the town, and a boy of six who will not be told why the games are over for a while" — costs nothing structurally and is the whole payoff the brief is chasing: a chronicle that remembers what a flag never could.

*Phases:* 1) **Phase 1 — replace the flag** (engine) — `ASKS.woman.yes` sets `g.family = { name, since:d.week }` instead of `g.flags=1`; its `need` reads `!g.family` instead of `!g.flags`; both branches route through `remember(d,g,"kept"/"refused")` like the other four ASKS entries instead of hand-rolling the regard delta. Zero new UI. Confirms the object persists and nothing else in the file chokes on `g.flags` disappearing (already confirmed: no other reader exists). 2) **Phase 2 — the thread can deepen** (both) — A per-man weekly conception-style roll (mirrors `bearChild`'s gate shape: elapsed-since-last, low weekly odds) adds `g.family.child = {born:d.week}` on men carrying `g.family`; a `childAge`-style helper and a small age-keyed narration table (2-3 unforced lines, no forced choice-gate — a yard has no rhetor/box/toga track) surface it in the chronicle the way `childYear` does for the domus, at one or two ages rather than four. 3) **Phase 3 — the walk-on-recruit arc** (both) — A `familyKin`-style event mirroring `kinWeek`/`raiseKin` structurally: gated on a thread-child having reached a floor age (draft-age analog to `kinWeek`'s pool filter), firing a grown-child-at-the-gate event that either takes up the father's `cls`/`kit` (father still active — a live legacy, not a memorial one) or arrives orphaned if the father died in the interim, reusing `g.sworn` and the trait-draw pattern from `KIN_TRAITS`. 4) **Phase 4 — the leverage and the reason to live** (both) — `poachTarget`/`startPoach`/`defect` read `g.family` when present: either it raises a man's poach-target weight (a family is something to protect, which cuts the ask's own "cuts both ways" line into an actual mechanic) or the `poached` arc's bait text branches on it ("a roof for her, free and clear" instead of only the standing freedom-in-three-years line). Separately, `AMBITIONS.freedom.press`/`despair` copy varies when `g.family` is set — no new ambition kind, just text and, optionally, a small defiance/despair-rate modifier keyed on the thread's presence. 5) **Phase 5 — the death line** (engine) — One `chron()` call added to `boutAftermath`'s `res.aDies` branch, alongside the existing `mournKin`/`kinReact`/`dropTies` calls, reading `g.family` if set and naming who is left. This is the smallest phase and the one the whole brief is actually chasing — ship it even if Phases 2-4 don't happen.

*Reuses:* `ASKS.woman` (13657-13664) as the seed trigger; `remember`/`REGARD`/`g.memory` (7294-7338) to fold the yes/no into the existing memory log instead of hand-mutating regard; `d.domus`'s `bearChild` (8047), `childAge`/`CHILD_YEARS`/`childYear` (8003, 8173-8199) as the shape to partially mirror for aging a thread-child, explicitly NOT `raiseEvent`/`togaEvent`/`resolveToga`/`daughterEvent` (those are ludus-succession-specific and don't apply to a man who owns nothing to inherit); `kinWeek`/`raiseKin`/`KIN_TRAITS`/`g.sworn` (14402-14432) as the direct precedent for a grown child walking in at the gate; `startPoach`/`poachTarget`/`defect`/`poachWeek`/the `poached` arc (12600-12671, 18320-18345) as the existing threat-lever to extend rather than a new hostile-action system; `AMBITIONS.freedom`/`WORDS.wants` (1719-1724, 13688-13701) for the second-reason-to-want-the-rudis hook; `boutAftermath`'s death branch and `mournKin`/`kinReact`/`dropTies` (17425-17457, 4493-4516) as the insertion point for the death line; `her(text,g)`/`PR(g)`/`isF(g)` (352-366) for gender-consistent text, since `ASKS.woman`'s `need` already has no `g.sex` gate.

**Risk.** The stated risk in the brief is exact and confirmed by the numbers already in the ask: `yes` currently pays +18 regard/+14 morale/+6 defiance for a single click with no ongoing cost, which makes it the single best-paying, lowest-friction ASKS entry in the table (compare `brother`'s +16 regard for a promise that can bind a future sell decision, or `burial`'s +8/+8 for an ongoing 3-denarii/week levy) — a rational player says yes every time it appears, and today that's the whole transaction. Turning it into a persisting object without also turning it into ongoing exposure just makes that flat win permanent instead of one-time — a strictly bigger free regard/morale/defiance grant with no offsetting downside, which is worse, not better, against "cruelty is permitted, never optimal": it would make kindness even more obviously the efficient play than it already is, with nothing pulling the other way. The guardrail is Phase 4: the thread has to be a poach-target multiplier and/or a despair-rate lever BEFORE it ships as a standalone feature, not as a someday-follow-up — a family with no matching liability is the flag bug with better prose. The build order in the phases above already sequences this (Phase 1's flag-replacement is safe alone since it's mechanically identical to today; Phases 2-3 must not ship without Phase 4's downside attached, or the interim state is a strict regression on the design value).

**Verify first.** Before Phase 2: instrument how often `ASKS.woman` actually fires and is accepted under a played house (the file's own `askWeek` comment at 13668-13684 already gives the base rate for the whole ASKS pool — 9.5% of men who ever qualify actually get asked anything, on 1.7% of weeks — so `woman` specifically, as the lowest-weighted of five candidates competing for that same 1.7%/week roll, is going to be rare; get the actual number before designing content depth against it). Before Phase 3: measure, the way `#226`'s comment measured the domus arc (8153-8172, "median of three lines... longest stretch running 91 weeks"), how many weeks a typical roster-lifetime thread-child needs to reach walk-on age against a gladiator's own median tenure/lifespan — if the man is dead or freed before the child would ever be draft-age under realistic pacing, Phase 3 is dead weight and the payoff should compress to Phase 5 (the death line) plus a foreshortened version of Phase 3 rather than a full age-gated pipeline. Before Phase 4: confirm `poachTarget`'s existing formula (`g.defiance + gladValue(g)/60`, 12604) actually correlates with men likely to hold `g.family` — if the highest-defiance men (the design's own "most dangerous to own") are disproportionately NOT the ones who'd have passed the `woman` ask's `regardOf(g)>=55` gate, the leverage hook has fewer real targets than the pitch implies, and that's a number to have before writing the poach-bait branching text.

**#240 — A Rival House Is a Family, Not a Slot** *(new system, discretionary)*
A rival lanista who dies at your hand or your table currently has no children: `bayRefill` sells his empty yard to a stranger from `NEW_HOUSES`, wiping every week of grudge or warmth the two houses built. Let him leave a son sometimes, one whose opening stance is earned by how his father's story actually ended — hot and vengeful off a `settleNemHouse` ruin, already warm off a `RIVAL_BEATS.end` retirement — so the antagonist side gets a sliver of the continuity `succeed()` already gives the player.

A rival house object, confirmed across its three construction sites (`makeRivals` line 6469, `bayRefill` line ~6913-6919, `FREEDMEN.lanista.run` line ~14315), is `{ name, fame, grudge, form, formTier, star, fighters }` plus whichever of `opened` (bayRefill only) or `freedFrom`/`bitter` (freedman-founded only) applies — no age field, no lineage field, on any of the three. `name` is not a person's name; it is a lookup key into the static `LANISTAE` table (`lanistaOf(h.name)`), so the house and "who runs it" are the same fixed record — there is no rival-side equivalent of `d.lanista` to swap out at all.

A house currently leaves play by exactly two `.retired = true` writes. One: `RIVAL_BEATS.end` (line 2244), gated on `met>=26 && years>=11 && warm>=52` — a long, amicable rivalry, where the rival lanista "sells up and takes the road to Nola." Two: `settleNemHouse(d, true)` with `nemEdge(d) >= 1` (line 12243) — a declared `nemHouse` feud won decisively, "he sells up and takes the road to Nola" again, this time broken rather than fond. Both are read by `liveRivals` (`h=>!h.retired`), and once live rivals drop under `BAY_FLOOR` (3), `bayRefill` — after a wait timed by `d.flags.bayDue` — installs a brand-new house from the static `NEW_HOUSES`/`LANISTAE` pool (Glaber, Cossutius, Marcellus, Rufinus, Pollio, Varro) with a fresh key, freshly rolled fame/grudge/fighters, and zero reference to the vacated identity. A grudge nursed for eighteen declared-feud weeks or a warmth built past `met>=26` is discarded outright.

The marriage mechanic the brief points to is real and precisely scoped: `weddingEndsFeud(d, hName)` sets `h.kin = true`, called from the rival branches of both `resolveMatch` and `resolveDaughter`. It is read in exactly one place — `declareNemHouse`'s candidate filter (`!h.kin`) — so it currently means "this house can never be re-declared a nemesis," full stop. It has no bearing on who succeeds the lanista, because nothing currently succeeds a rival lanista at all.

At both `.retired = true` sites, roll whether the house passes to a son instead of vacating for `bayRefill`. On a hit, the house object survives under the same `name` key (so `d.rivals`, `d.metHouse[h.name]`, and any open deadlines keep resolving against it) but gains a heir-identity override — a generated name plus a `LANISTAE`-shaped dial set (`grudgeDecay`, `poach`, `bribe`, `train`, `bid`, `stature`, optionally `sabotage`) nudged from the father's, since `lanistaOf` currently has no override layer to check before falling back to the static table. `h.fighters` and a fraction of `h.fame` carry over — the roster and the name Capua knows, not the father's numbers wholesale, mirroring how `succeed()` applies `HEIRS.son.fameKeep:0.72` rather than handing the new lanista the old one's exact standing.

The son's opening `grudge`/`warm` replace the flat defaults every fresh house gets (`makeRivals`: `grudge:ri(0,10)`; `bayRefill`: `grudge:ri(0,12)`, `warm` unset, reads as 0 via `houseOf`/`warmMove`). A son off a `settleNemHouse` ruin starts hot: high grudge, `warm` near zero, dials pushed toward `poach`/`sabotage`. A son off a `RIVAL_BEATS.end` retirement starts already warm — seeded well above the 0 every stranger house opens at — with lower grudge. If the father's arc carried `h.kin` (set by `weddingEndsFeud`), the son inherits it, so a marriage that "folds up a feud" stays folded for the next generation instead of resetting to a strange house's cold default.

*Phases:* 1) **Heir roll at the two exit doors** (engine) — A rollRivalHeir(d, h, mode) call inserted into RIVAL_BEATS.end's hit (line 2244, mode:'warm') and settleNemHouse's decisive-win branch (line 12243, mode:'broken'), gated on h.fighters.length>0 and a low-probability roll, so retirement without an heir (falling through to bayRefill as today) stays the common case. 2) **An identity override lanistaOf can read** (engine) — Since lanistaOf(h.name) is today a pure static LANISTAE[key] lookup with no per-house override, add an optional h.heir sub-object {name, trait, blurb, grudgeDecay, poach, bribe, train, bid, stature, sabotage, of, since} that lanistaOf checks before falling back to LANISTAE; names drawn from the same PRAENOMINA/NOMINA/COGNOMINA pools nameHeir already uses for the player's own nephew/scion. 3) **Stance and inheritance from how the father ended** (engine) — On a heir hit, set h.grudge/h.warm/h.formTier from mode ('broken': high grudge, near-zero warm, dials pushed toward poach/sabotage; 'warm': seeded warm well above a fresh house's 0, low grudge) instead of the flat ri(0,10-12) defaults in makeRivals/bayRefill; apply a fame-keep multiplier to h.fame the way HEIRS.son.fameKeep does for the player; carry h.kin forward untouched if the father's arc set it via weddingEndsFeud. 4) **Chronicle the handover and give it somewhere to point** (content) — A chron()/rivalLog entry at the moment of the roll (two variants, broken vs warm), reusing the same d.rivalLog side channel RIVAL_MOVES and NEM_BEATS already narrate weekly rival activity through; a small h.lineage record ({name, fame, endedAs, week}) scoped to the house, the rival-side analogue of d.forebears, so the rival panel/league table has something to show for the succession. 5) **Backfill for existing saves** (engine) — A migrate() step, following the {at:N, why, run(S)} pattern already used at 'the rivals grew a form and a warmth toward you' (line 9095), initializing h.heir:null, h.lineage:[] on every rival house and h.opened on the three founding RIVAL_SEED houses (currently only bayRefill-made houses carry it, and it is read nowhere else in the file) so old saves and new ones share the same shape.

*Reuses:* RIVAL_BEATS.end (line 2244) and settleNemHouse's decisive-win branch (line 12243) as the two roll sites; liveRivals/BAY_FLOOR/bayRefill/NEW_HOUSES as the fallback path when the roll misses; LANISTAE and lanistaOf(h.name) as the identity table the override must sit in front of; weddingEndsFeud's h.kin flag as the heritable marriage signal; HEIRS/heirEligible/nameHeir/succeed and d.forebears as the direct structural template (fameKeep/favorKeep-style multipliers, a generated name from PRAENOMINA/NOMINA/COGNOMINA, a lineage record pushed on transition); d.rivalLog/chron/nemLog as the narration channel; the migrate() array's {at:N, why, run(S)} convention for the additive save-compat step.

**Risk.** The named risk in the brief — a buyable soft heir — is avoidable structurally: the roll must live only inside the two existing `.retired = true` writes, take no gold or player-chosen action, and both writes already sit behind real, slow, unpaid gates (`met>=26 && years>=11 && warm>=52` earned through free weekly `RIVAL_BEATS` rolls, or an entire won `nemHouse` feud arc, `NEM_MIN_RUN=18` weeks minimum). `makePeace` — the one denarii-for-grudge lever that exists (`peacePrice`/`makePeace`) — never sets `.retired`, so there is no coin-based path into either roll to firewall against; the guardrail is simply never adding one.

The subtler risk is arena-facing rather than player-facing: `bayRefill`'s own comment frames a stranger buying the empty yard as a feature — "a yard in Capua does not sit empty" — because turnover keeps the bay's threats varied. If the heir roll fires too often, most retirements stop feeding `NEW_HOUSES` and the bay converges on a small number of dynasties running the same dials generation after generation, which cuts against the game's own churn. Guardrail: keep the roll rare (a fraction of retirements, not a coin flip) and let it compete honestly with the `bayRefill` wait timer rather than pre-empting it.

**Verify first.** test/probes/feud.mjs already tags every nemHouse-feud ending with a taxonomy that includes "RUINED — you beat him and he sold up" and "he folded on his own" (rh.retired without a nemWon increment) — extend its per-house loop to also log every h.retired transition directly (by watching (d.rivals||[]) for the flag flipping, not only inside an active `cur` feud window), because RIVAL_BEATS.end can fire on a house that was never a declared nemHouse feud at all, so the probe's existing `ends` tally does not currently capture the peaceful door in that case. No probe touches bayRefill/NEW_HOUSES at all (grepped test/ for both, no hits), so pair that with a fresh count of how many campaign-life retirements resolve through bayRefill (a stranger) versus would resolve through a heir roll at a few candidate probabilities.

The falsifier: if either `.retired=true` site fires only a handful of times across a long played campaign (the file's own #225 note already cites 6 wins out of 18 declared nemHouse feuds over 2,822 probed weeks for the "ruined" door), the mechanic is a rare, legible beat as intended and worth the two-phase engine lift. If it turns out to fire only in single digits across an entire multi-decade campaign, there may not be enough occurrences for a player to ever notice the difference, and the two engine phases (the identity-override layer in particular) are not worth their own weight for content nobody sees twice.

**#241 — Endow, Actually** *(overhaul, discretionary)*
MONUMENTS.endow currently buys +1.1 acclaim a week for 44,000d — the same flat-bonus shape as colossus's +6 fame and arena's +10 crowd — while its blurb claims a self-funding annual games that never gets built. Make it build the thing it's already claiming: a seventh, house-owned CALENDAR entry that produces a real card through the exact pipeline the other six already use.

MONUMENTS.endow (src/ludus.jsx ~15341): cost 44000, upkeep 34, years 3, tier 2 (opens once monuReady(d) — all five WORKS finished), perk:"acclaim", n:1.1. Its blurb claims "games that hold themselves, funded out of a sum so large the interest alone pays for blood every year after you are gone," and its done-text claims "games in your name now that will run when your grandsons are old." The only place workPerk(d,"acclaim") is consumed is worksWeek() (~15471): `d.acclaim = clamp((d.acclaim||0) + workPerk(d,"acclaim"), 0, 100)` — a flat permanent weekly tick, structurally identical to colossus's fame perk and capua's fame perk. Grepping the full 31k-line source for the literal string "endow" turns up exactly one hit outside the MONUMENTS table and the generic ALL_WORK_KEYS/workPerk loops: nothing. It never calls festivalNow, never touches CALENDAR (the fixed 6-entry, 18-week festival table at ~2572: quinquatria/floralia/apollinares/vulcanalia/romani/saturnalia, "the year recurs, so it can be planned around"), never calls makeGames. No game is ever staged. This is the same fault class the source's own audit already logged three lines above this very entry: the tomb monument's blurb ("and a death costs the cells less") credited an effect to the cells that `collSoften` produces, not the tomb's actual `regard` perk — flagged in-source as "a claim about the state that the state does not hold." Endow's case is worse: it doesn't misattribute an effect, it advertises a mechanism (a recurring, self-staging festival) that doesn't exist in any form.

Once workDone(d,"endow") is true, the house's effective festival year gains a seventh entry: a CALENDAR-shaped object (same fields as the six: w, key, name, month, blurb, purse/fame multipliers, tier, offers, force-engine flags) on a fixed, unclaimed week of the 18-week clock, folded in by a new `calendarFor(d)` accessor rather than by mutating the base CALENDAR constant. Because festivalNow/makeGames already treat "the festival this week" as a generic F object — reading F.purse, F.fame, F.tier, F.offers, F.forceMelee/forceHunt/forceNaum, F.noSine, F.crowd, F.deathCost, F.gear with no per-key special-casing beyond one probabilistic check against F.key==="romani" — a new entry produces real opponent offers, real purses, real venues through venueFor/skyFor with essentially no new bout-resolution code. And because succeed() (the succession handler, ~7938) never touches d.works, the seventh festival survives every generational handover automatically, for free — the same way colossus's fame bonus or the tomb's regard bonus already do. "Games in your name" is then literally true three generations later, without inventing a second thing that has to be maintained in parallel.

*Phases:* 1) **Wire the seventh slot** (engine) — Add a house-conditional CALENDAR-shaped entry, exposed only through a new calendarFor(d) accessor (CALENDAR itself stays the fixed six). Repoint the five call sites that decide what festival a given week is — festivalNow (~2618), nextFestivals (~2620), the forward-planner calendarRows (~13297), the in-fight festival lookup CALENDAR.find(x=>x.key===d.games.fest) (~17628), and the 18-block year-strip in the UI's year panel (~22786) — from the bare CALENDAR constant to calendarFor(d). makeGames, weeksUntil, venueFor, skyFor need no changes; they already consume whatever object festivalNow hands back. 2) **Write the festival card** (content) — Pick one of the twelve weeks CALENDAR doesn't already use (1,3,4,6,7,9,10,12,13,15,16,18) and write name/month/blurb plus a purse/fame/tier/offers profile sized to a 44,000d, tier-2 spend — closer to apollinares/romani in scale than floralia. These numbers don't exist in the source yet and are drafts for playtesting, not verified facts. Rewrite MONUMENTS.endow's blurb, done and say strings (rendered verbatim in the Monuments panel at ~23124/23155) to describe what the purchase now does. 3) **Retire or re-earn the flat acclaim tick** (engine) — Decide what happens to the existing perk:"acclaim", n:1.1 consumed by worksWeek (~15471). Acclaim already has other sources (bout-appetite payouts ~5358, the licensing event ~2562, monument-completion bonus ~15463), so it isn't orphaned by removing the passive tick. Recommended: drop or shrink the flat weekly grant and instead award acclaim on wins at the new endowed festival specifically, so the number is earned by the mechanic rather than printed regardless of outcome — otherwise endow both gains a new festival AND keeps stacking the old flat bonus, over-valuing it against colossus/arena/capua at similar cost. 4) **Chronicle and copy pass** (content) — Add a chron() line the first time the endowed week's card goes up each year (parallel to the existing "Games are announced — X!" line ~19742), using yearOf(d) so it can name which running this is. Update the CALENDAR header comment ("Six festivals in their real order", ~2570) and the "six festivals" note at ~6190 to acknowledge the conditional seventh. Confirm calendarRows and the year-strip only light the new week up for houses that hold it.

*Reuses:* CALENDAR, festivalNow, nextFestivals, weeksUntil, makeGames (its generic F-object contract: w/key/name/month/blurb/purse/fame/tier/offers/forceMelee/forceHunt/forceNaum/noSine/allSine/crowd/deathCost/gear/fineBonus/rest), venueFor, skyFor, workDone, workOpen, workPerk, worksWeek, MONUMENTS.endow, calendarRows, chron, and the fact that succeed() leaves d.works untouched (confirmed by reading succeed(), ~7938-7992) — the mechanism that already lets every other monument's perk survive succession for free.

**Risk.** Named risk from the brief is real and specific: this must stay exactly one CALENDAR-shaped object behind exactly one seam (calendarFor), never a second array, a second festivalNow, or player-facing controls for picking the endowed week/type — that's the munus system's job already (MUNUS_OCCASIONS/MUNUS_SCALES/SPECTACLES, ~6260 on), and duplicating any of it here is the scope creep the brief warns against. Guardrail: the new entry gets zero bespoke fields beyond what the six existing CALENDAR members already use, and zero new UI beyond what calendarRows/festivalNow/the year-strip already render generically. Second, narrower risk: because CALENDAR festivals only ever generate offers — nothing in makeGames assigns fighters to a bout, the player chooses who (if anyone) goes — a seventh recurring festival doesn't force additional combat exposure on men who didn't choose it, so on inspection it doesn't cut against "the arena is the antagonist" or "men are not units" any more than the existing six already do. Guardrail is simply parity: give the endowed festival's offers identical accept/decline and roster rules to the base six, no auto-accept, no forced assignment — an opportunity, never an obligation.

**Verify first.** (1) Reachability: measure, using the same late-game trajectory data the "THE LONG MIDDLE" note already establishes (gold to 27,569/week by week ~X in a measured house), what fraction of houses that reach monuReady(d) actually build endow specifically versus spending on colossus/arena/capua instead — if effectively nobody finishes it in real play, phases 2-4 are effort spent on content nobody sees. (2) Slot collision: with the new entry occupying 1 of 18 weeks, confirm across a simulated run that festivalNow's single CALENDAR.find/calendarFor.find never has two legitimate claimants the same week, and that it doesn't sit inside the 6-week MUNUS_COOL window in a way that makes the player's own munus and the endowed festival compete for the same week type. (3) Balance falsifier: measure whether a 7th, apollinares/romani-scale festival materially raises death rate or fatigue burden per house-year against today's six, and whether the added purse/fame at a 44,000d price point is worth that — the same "measured across N houses" standard the tomb/regard and fame-ladder audits already used elsewhere in this source, not an assumption. (4) Succession falsifier: confirm in an actual second-generation save (not by inspection alone) that a scion who inherits mid-build or post-completion sees the seventh festival appear on schedule with no extra migration needed.

**THE QUEUE.** All twenty-five stand open. Struck through as they ship, with the release that did:

The unsigned half was exact: 0 of 2,582 beats named a god) · ~~#220~~ (v3.178.0 — three of the four are surfaced already and the pact is taken twice a house; the gambit is the one that was dark, 0% of 94.2% available weeks, and the arc to hang it on is 2.6%, not 79%) · ~~#221~~ (v3.179.0 — the premise was #208's dead median; the claim survives corrected and worse: five men in six never cross a career gate, and a first bout was worth a tenth of a chronicle line)

Top-10 share 21.6% → 13.6%) · ~~#224~~ (v3.167.0 — the headline was the rope's artifact; the real fault was that never answering beat every answer on the list) · ~~#225~~ (v3.168.0 — headline right, diagnosis blamed the respawn; the fault was that a feud could not be LOST. 77.1% of weeks → 36.3%, six grudge matches a feud → one) · ~~#226~~ (v3.169.0 — right, and the heir was a son the house had never had: `heirEligible` read the lanista's age and never his household. The calendar now forces the engines it never could) · ~~#229~~ (v3.173.0 — true, and understated: the agenda warned a dying house on 1.7% of its short weeks and told it to go building on 57.1%) · ~~#230~~ (v3.174.0 — the counter measures which CARD was taken, not what the sand rolled; the real fault was the town breaking `wantStakes`) · ~~#231~~ (v3.175.0 — three limbs already answered; the fourth it did not name: the word banded `rateMan` and the sand rolls `winChance`, so "even, near enough" was a bout lost two times in three)


Asked for as five ledgers — gameplay, graphics, depth, story, mechanics — five items each. Not a
defect hunt: the question this time is what a player *meets*. Measured with the new `survey` probe
(**16 houses × 420 weeks, 3,961 house-weeks, 1,046 men**, under the reference lanista), a follow-up
arc count (12 × 360, 3,629 weeks), a re-run of `dark` (8 × 320, 1,942 weeks, 1,849 bouts),
`coverage`, and a screenshot pass over a founding house, a fought bout, and a forged year-27 house.
Where a figure depends on the reference player's *policy* rather than the game, the item says
**(rope)** — a system the rope does not pursue reads dark without being dark, and acting on one of
those begins with one more probe, not with code.

**THE FRAME, before the items — how sixteen long houses actually went.** Endings: **7 in debt, 3 to
rebellion, 1 to ruin, 5 survived** to week 420; the dead died at a median of about year 3. Median
gold by era: **991 → 4,163 → 4,361 → 3,480** — flat after year four. Median fame: **145 → 1,727 →
3,053 → 3,848** — climbing forever. Of 1,046 men who ever stood in the cells, **the median career
is one bout and zero wins** (p90 ten bouts); 470 died, 45%. A feud stood on **79% of all weeks**.
The saga reached its finale **0 times in 13 tellings**. Rome was offered **0 times**. The
chronicle's most-told sentence was told **616 times — 15.6% of every week the sixteen houses
lived**.

#### THE GAMEPLAY LEDGER

**#207 — SHIPPED v3.156.0, HALF-REFUTED on its own follow-up.** The liturgy already engages on 64%
of weeks and the median weekly net runs −23/−58/−68/−126 by era — the late game is a treadmill, not
a coast. What survived: deaths cluster at years 1–4 where step-costs grow undisclosed, and under it
a real bug — `weeklyBill` was missing the medicus's and armourer's wages. See the v3.156.0 entry.
*As opened:* The difficulty curve is upside down: the hardest week is around week 30 and the easiest is
week 300. Debt is the game's dominant death — 7 of 16 houses, median about year 3 — while the
survivors coast on a flat ~4,000d median from year 4 onward with nothing pressing them. The young
house's squeeze is the game working as designed; the old house's calm is not. Recommend moving
pressure late rather than softening it early: a famous house should be *billed* like one — expected
to stage games, touched for liturgies (the liturgy exists), leaned on by the aedile — so the ledger
stays a live instrument after year four instead of a solved one.

**#208 — CLOSED, REFUTED: the figure was the survey's own artifact** (470 fallen summaries counted
as zero-bout careers). True: dead-median 4–5 bouts, 88–90% debut survival, flat 10–15% per-bout
hazard, fame protection real and saturating. See the close above the audit. *As opened:* The median
man fights once and wins nothing.** p50 career: 1 bout, 0 wins; p90: 10. 45% of
every man who ever entered the cells died there or on the sand. Buying is the loop and fighting is
the point, yet half the roster never really reaches it. Partly the rope buying fodder **(rope)** —
but the economy makes fodder optimal, which is the finding. Recommend a designed novice road:
survivable debut formats (exhibition, wooden-sword cards — the yard tournament already exists as
